key_insight: A target-ω model damps interfacial turbulence in stratified gas–liquid flow without calibration against target data, while reducing near-interface grid sensitivity relative to an Egorov-type formulation.
engineering_relevance: The formulation supports RANS predictions of gas-side flow and turbulence in stratified two-phase systems, including coupled liquid-depth prediction.
method: Embed interfacial damping in a low-Reynolds-number Wilcox-type k–ω model within a one-field RANS/VOF framework.
Construct a gas-side target ω from an effective interfacial wall coordinate based on the local resolved flow.
Use power-law blending for a smooth transition between viscous and logarithmic limits.
evidence_signal: Assessment against three gas-layer DNS cases at Reτ ≈ 180 and the Fabre co-current and Stäbler counter-current experiments showed generally good gas-side predictions and close agreement with measured liquid depth in the Stäbler case.
watch_item: Some grid dependence remains on the coarsest mesh, and validation is limited to the resolved-interface conditions studied.
paper_title: Development and assessment of a target-$ω$ interfacial turbulence-damping model for stratified gas--liquid flow
